Hi Samantha — thanks for the questions. TL;DR answers first, then a short explanation and a sample config snippet. I’ll also attach redwood-sample-config.yaml with the fields called out.

TL;DR
- Static egress IPs: For hosted customers we publish regional egress IP blocks you can allowlist; for strict isolation you can use Redwood Private (VPC peering or PrivateLink) and keep traffic inside your network.
- DNS: Private endpoints resolve to customer-facing CNAMEs that ultimately map to Redwood-managed IPs. When using PrivateLink we give you an interface endpoint that keeps traffic on your VPC and resolves to private ENIs. Behavior varies by option (summary below).
- mTLS: Supported. For Private deployments we recommend mTLS with client certs; you can upload your certs (PEM) or use our provisioning flow if you prefer Redwood-managed cert rotation. Hosted API can use TLS + API keys or mTLS if you opt into client certs.
- SDK auth: We support static API keys, short-lived JWT tokens (via an STS exchange using your IdP), and mutual TLS. The SDK example shows how to rotate keys and use a short-lived bearer token.

Details
1) Hosted + allowlist: If you remain on Hosted API, we can provide a set of regional egress IP ranges (example: 34.210.0.0/20, 52.42.16.0/22) — these are what our NATs use. We publish them and update with advanced notice. This is easiest for firewall allowlists but does require you accept our published ranges.

2) PrivateLink / Interface Endpoint: We can provide an AWS PrivateLink endpoint. This creates an ENI in your account and traffic stays on the AWS backbone. DNS will resolve to the interface endpoint (private IPs in your subnet). This is the most provably private option and avoids opening public egress.

3) VPC Peering / Customer egress: If you prefer routing through your NAT, you can peer or route to Redwood and egress through your own NAT — in that case you control the public egress IPs, and we only need the internal routing + port allowances.

4) mTLS options: For mTLS we accept x509 client certs signed by your PKI. You can either upload the cert chain via our console (Private) or we can set up an automated rotation with your internal CA via ACME-ish integration (requires ops coordination).

Sample SDK snippet (illustrative, see attached YAML for full example):

---redwood-sample-config.yaml---
api:
  auth_mode: "short-lived-token"  # options: api_key | short-lived-token | mTLS
  token_endpoint: "https://auth.redwood.com/v1/token"
network:
  connectivity: "privatelink"  # options: privatelink | hosted_allowlist | peer_egress
  privatelink:
    service_name: "com.redwood.inference.us-west-2"
    interface_subnets: ["subnet-0abc123", "subnet-0def456"]
  allowlist_ranges: ["34.210.0.0/20"]
---end---

What I’ll attach
- redwood-sample-config.yaml with comments for each field.
- Short doc describing the PrivateLink provisioning steps and the expected lead time (typically 3–5 business days to provision and validate).

Next step

If it helps, I can also provide a minimal allowlist if you want to do a short proof-of-concept without PrivateLink first.
